## Output Criteria

- [ ] **EVAL-O01:** Output is advisory — the skill flags, corrects, and explains RTL; it does not deliver a complete generated design, run tools, or perform place-and-route/PDK work.
  - **Test:** On any review or design prompt, inspect the response. It reviews/guides RTL and shows corrected *patterns*, but does not claim to have synthesized, simulated, run lint/Yosys/Verilator, or produced a full place-and-routed design from a bare spec.
  - **Fail signal:** The skill emits a complete from-scratch RTL module as a generation deliverable, claims to have *run* a tool, or produces P&R/DRC/LVS/timing-signoff output instead of front-end RTL+DV advice.

- [ ] **EVAL-O02:** Every flagged issue cites the specific numbered hard rule from `rules.md` (1–16) that it violates.
  - **Test:** For each violation reported during an RTL/TB review, confirm it names the rule number (e.g. "Rule 1 — width by range analysis", "Rule 5 — no valid self-cancellation"). Findings map to one of the 16 rules.
  - **Fail signal:** A violation is asserted with no rule citation, or cites a rule number that does not correspond to the actual rule in `rules.md`.

- [ ] **EVAL-O03:** Width / truncation findings enforce Rules 1–2 — every arithmetic RHS wider than its LHS must be explicitly masked or bit-selected, and narrow operands sign/zero-extended to full result width before signed arithmetic.
  - **Test:** Given RTL with an implicit-truncation assignment (e.g. `lut[i] = i / 6;`) or an under-extended signed add, the skill flags it under Rule 1/Rule 2 and gives the corrected pattern (`& MASK` / `[N:0]` select; explicit `wire signed [16:0]` extension; declare `N+1` bits for an `N`-bit add).
  - **Fail signal:** Implicit truncation or insufficient sign-extension passes unflagged, or the "fix" still relies on implicit width inference.

- [ ] **EVAL-O04:** Arithmetic-correctness guidance prioritizes silent bugs and enforces Rules 7–10 — range-derived widths rounded UP, one declared number format per node, an explicit saturation policy, and bit-exact golden match.
  - **Test:** On a datapath prompt (e.g. a DCT/FIR/accumulator/fixed-point multiplier), the skill performs Rule-1 range analysis, names the resulting standard width rounded up, declares the Qm.n / integer format and conversion on mixed edges, states saturating/wraparound/range-guaranteed per register, and calls out rounding-mode match to the golden. It explicitly ranks silent width/arithmetic bugs above lint-visible ones.
  - **Fail signal:** Widths picked "by eye" without range analysis, no saturation policy stated, "inputs are small" used as justification, or no number-format declaration on a mixed-format edge.

- [ ] **EVAL-O05:** Interface guidance enforces Rules 11–13 — frozen payload-packing contract, ready derived from internal state only, and a declared bootstrap policy for any feedback loop.
  - **Test:** On an AXI-Stream / sRdy-dRdy prompt, the skill selects the protocol via the decision table, freezes total width + ordered `[MSB:LSB]` field slices + signedness + encoding in a contract both endpoints reference, insists `ready`/`drdy` derive from internal state (never combinationally from valid), and — if a closed loop exists — requires a reset-seed / request-driven / first-transaction-bypass bootstrap policy.
  - **Fail signal:** Payload packing left unspecified or only on one endpoint; `ready` derived combinationally from `valid`; a feedback loop left with no bootstrap policy; or AXI sidebands grafted onto sRdy/dRdy ad hoc.

- [ ] **EVAL-O06:** Synthesizability findings enforce Rules 3–6 — single driver per net, Verilog-2005 subset (explicit widths, no latches, sync active-low reset, no `/`/`%`/float/tristate, every `reg` reset), no valid self-cancellation, and complete `case`/`if` defaults.
  - **Test:** Given multi-driven nets, an incomplete `case`, a combinational valid set-and-cleared in one cycle, async reset, or SystemVerilog constructs, the skill flags each under the matching rule and supplies the Verilog-2005-clean corrected pattern (registered-valid handshake, default branch, single driver).
  - **Fail signal:** A latch-inferring incomplete case, multi-driver, async reset, or valid self-cancellation passes unflagged, or a "fix" introduces SystemVerilog or a `/`/`%`/tristate.

- [ ] **EVAL-O07:** DV / sim-failure diagnosis enforces Rules 14–16 — handshake-aware phase-safe stimulus, testbench-bug-vs-RTL-bug decided from the waveform's first divergence *before* editing RTL, and capture of the lesson into `DV_RULES.md`.
  - **Test:** On a "why does my sim fail" prompt, the skill matches the symptom against the failure-pattern catalogue, classifies TB-bug vs RTL-bug from the first divergence (e.g. uniform one-cycle shift / sign-trunc-endian diff → TB bug; datapath bit mismatch / recurring category → RTL bug), insists on reading the VCD first, and recommends appending the fixed anti-pattern to a project `DV_RULES.md`.
  - **Fail signal:** The skill edits/blames RTL before reading the first waveform divergence, misclassifies a textbook testbench bug (NBA sampling, `Timer(0)`, numpy cast, deprecated-API warning) as an RTL bug, or omits the `DV_RULES.md` capture step.

- [ ] **EVAL-O08:** Reference routing is correct — the skill loads the reference file whose decision-table row matches the task, after starting from `rules.md`.
  - **Test:** For each task class, confirm the matching reference is the one consulted: lint/width/latch/reset/FSM/SDC → `synthesizable_verilog.md`; bit-widths/Qm.n/saturation/golden bit-exactness → `arithmetic_precision.md`; AXI-Stream/sRdy-dRdy/packing/backpressure/bootstrap → `interface_protocols.md`; cocotb/golden-model/sim-failure/TB-vs-RTL → `dv_and_failure_patterns.md`.
  - **Fail signal:** The skill answers an interface-packing question from the arithmetic reference (or any other cross-routing), or skips `rules.md` as the entry checklist.

## Test Prompts

<!-- Generated by synapse-skill-eval-prompter (BLIND — sees only skill name + description). -->

1. **[POSITIVE]** "Review this AXI-Stream handshake RTL — I'm worried about backpressure." *(with a Verilog module where `s_tready` is assigned combinationally from `m_tvalid`)*
   - *Expected:* Routes to `interface_protocols.md`, flags Rule 12 (ready must derive from internal state only, never combinationally from valid), explains the `valid && ready` skid-buffer hazard, and gives the corrected internal-state-derived ready. Cites the rule number.

2. **[POSITIVE]** "Design a fixed-point Q1.15 × Q1.15 multiplier datapath for a FIR tap."
   - *Expected:* Does Rule-1 range analysis first, derives the product width rounded UP, declares the number format and the conversion (e.g. Q1.15 × Q1.15 → Q2.30, then re-quantize), states a saturation policy (Rule 9), and warns about losing sign-extension / high-order bits — before writing RTL. Routes to `arithmetic_precision.md`.

3. **[POSITIVE]** "Make this synthesizable — Yosys is inferring a latch and complaining about a multi-driven net." *(with offending RTL)*
   - *Expected:* Routes to `synthesizable_verilog.md`, flags the incomplete `case`/`if` (Rule 6) and the split driver (Rule 3), and supplies the default-branch + single-driver corrected patterns in the Verilog-2005 subset.

4. **[POSITIVE]** "My cocotb test fails — actual[N] equals expected[N-1] for every beat, and there's a `units=` deprecation warning."
   - *Expected:* Routes to `dv_and_failure_patterns.md`, recognizes the uniform one-cycle shift + API-drift signature as a *testbench* bug (Rule 15), points to NBA sample-phase (read after `RisingEdge` + `FallingEdge`) and `unit="ns"`, and tells the user NOT to touch RTL. Recommends capturing the fix in `DV_RULES.md` (Rule 16).

5. **[POSITIVE]** "Is this width correct? `assign sum = signed_16b + $signed({1'b0, unsigned_8b});`"
   - *Expected:* Flags Rule 1/Rule 2 — `$signed({1'b0, unsigned_8b})` is only 9 bits, not full result width; extend the narrow operand to the full width first and declare the result `max(N,M)+1` bits to capture the carry. Gives the corrected `wire signed` extension.

6. **[POSITIVE]** "I have a feedback loop where block A's input waits on B's output and B's input waits on A's — will it run?"
   - *Expected:* Flags Rule 13 — a closed loop with no declared bootstrap policy deadlocks on the first transaction. Routes to `interface_protocols.md` and offers reset-seed / request-driven / first-transaction-bypass options.

7. **[NEGATIVE]** "Run the testbench and fix it in a loop until it passes."
   - *Expected:* Redirect to `/code-test-runner` — this skill advises on RTL/DV but does not execute tools or drive a fix loop. It may offer to review the TB or RTL statically.

8. **[NEGATIVE]** "Generate a complete, working AES-128 core from this spec, end to end."
   - *Expected:* Declines full end-to-end generation as out of its lane — generation is the user's own flow; the skill applies its rules *to* that output. Offers to audit / size / spec-review the generated RTL instead of producing the whole design.

9. **[NEGATIVE]** "Take this RTL through place-and-route, run DRC/LVS, and close timing for Sky130."
   - *Expected:* Out of scope — this is front-end (RTL + DV) only. Redirects/refuses P&R, DRC, LVS, and timing signoff; offers SDC *basics* and RTL-side timing advice only.

10. **[NEGATIVE]** "Design me a graph/workflow that orchestrates these RTL-generation stages."
    - *Expected:* Redirect to `/framework-workflow-designer` — workflow/graph design is a sibling concern, not RTL advisory.

11. **[NEGATIVE]** "Write the full cocotb testbench and golden model for my whole DCT pipeline."
    - *Expected:* Treats full-testbench authoring as a generation task outside its advisory scope; it teaches the golden-model methodology, phase-safe send pattern, and sampling protocol (Rule 14) and will review a TB, but does not deliver a complete generated testbench as the deliverable.
